subject: Prospect Q&A: Processing locations, subprocessors, and deletion workflow
messages:
From: Sam Porter <sam.porter@brooklinehealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Anna Liu <anna.liu@brooklinehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on where data is processed + deletion controls

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the demo last week. Before we proceed to an internal security review, Legal and IT have asked for clarifications on three items:

1) Where exactly will Brookline Health customer content be processed geographically (primary region and any failover/sojourn locations)?
2) Which subprocessors will touch or transit our data (indexing, logging, metrics, backups) and where are they located?
3) Walk us through your deletion workflow — how customer-triggered deletion is executed, how long artifacts (logs, backups, cached KV) persist, and proof that deleted data is scrubbed from backups/replicas.

Can you provide a short summary and any evidence artifacts (subprocessor list, deletion flow diagram, any policies) we can share with our InfoSec folks? If needed we can schedule a 30-min follow-up.

Appreciate it,
Sam

Sam Porter
Head of IT Security
Brookline Health

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Sam Porter <sam.porter@brooklinehealth.com>
Cc: Anna Liu <anna.liu@brooklinehealth.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on where data is processed + deletion controls

Hi Sam — thanks, and great questions. High-level answers below; I attached our current subprocessor inventory (redacted where needed) and a deletion flow diagram. More detail follows in a longer thread — I'll loop in infra and compliance on the specifics.

- Primary processing region: US West (us-west-2) for your tenant by default; customers can pin to us-east-1 or EU (eu-west-1) for Dedicated/Private plans.
- Sojourns / failover: we maintain short-lived sojourns in a secondary US region for failover (encrypted in transit and at rest). We do not route production inference payloads through jurisdictions outside the set you select, unless a customer opts into multi-region routing.
- Subprocessors: attached PDF lists compute providers, logging/metrics vendors, and backup/archive providers. We classify subprocessors by role and transfer boundary.
- Deletion flow: customer-initiated deletion triggers immediate logical deletion from primary stores; KV cache eviction is triggered asynchronously; backups are tagged and scheduled for purging per retention windows. We provide an auditable deletion token and evidence (screenshot of deletion job run) upon request.

I'm copying Marcus (infrastructure) and Neha (compliance) to add specifics on retention windows, backup snapshots, and cross-border transfer exceptions.

Would you prefer a one-pager or a sandbox demonstration showing the deletion event?

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_subprocessor_list_2027-06.pdf
Attachment: deletion-flow-diagram.png

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Sam Porter <sam.porter@brooklinehealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on where data is processed + deletion controls

Sam, quick technical notes to complement Hannah's summary:

- Processing surfaces: inference happens on dedicated model runtime instances inside the region you select (default us-west-2). Auxiliary processing (indexing for embeddings, async evals) runs in a controlled batch environment that is region-bound to the customer region unless the customer authorizes cross-region async jobs.

- Short-lived sojourns: we replicate small operational metadata (routing keys, cache tokens) to a single warm standby region for failover; payloads are never intentionally copied outside the configured regions. Sojourn retention is kept to under 24 hours for failover scenarios.

- Subprocessors: the attached list includes our compute partner (MajorCloud GPU Instances — US-based), metrics/logging (Observix — data plane in US), backups (VaultStor — multi-region but customer-bounded), and monitoring (TraceQ — processed telemetry is sampled and pseudonymized). Each subprocessor entry includes their country of operations and the legal basis for processing (contract + SCCs where applicable).

- Backups and deletion: backups are incremental snapshots stored with VaultStor. When a deletion request is raised, we create a purge job that marks snapshots for retention removal — purge completes within the maximum backup window (default 30 days for hosted plans). For requests requiring faster removal (e.g., contractual obligations), we offer an accelerated purge service with attestation.

Neha, can you confirm the standard retention windows and the attestation template we provide for accelerated deletion?

—Marcus

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Sam Porter <sam.porter@brooklinehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 09:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on where data is processed + deletion controls

Hi all — adding compliance specifics so Brookline has what it needs for audit: 

- Standard retention windows (hosted): inference logs = 90 days (configurable); metrics aggregates = 365 days (retained for product analytics); backups/snapshots = 30 days by default.
- Deletion evidence: we provide a deletion token and an audit log entry (timestamp, operator, job id). For backup purges we provide a purge job id and completion time. If Brookline requires a formal attestation (e.g., for procurement or contract), we can supply a signed Certificate of Data Deletion within our enterprise plan SLA.

- Cross-border transfers: by default, we do not transfer content outside the customer-chosen region except for the limited failover sojourn described by Marcus. When a transfer is required (e.g., customer enables multi-region routing), we use SCCs and ensure subprocessors execute under GDPR-compliant terms; Data Processing Addendum (DPA) covers specifics.

- Evidence artifacts attached: redwood_subprocessor_list_2027-06.pdf (with geographies), deletion-flow-diagram.png, and an example deletion-audit-sample.txt (redacted) — happy to provide a fuller set under NDA if needed.

Sam/Anna — would you like us to mark these artifacts as "evidence for procurement" and send them to your compliance intake mailbox, or would a live walkthrough with Neha and Marcus be better?

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Privacy & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: deletion-audit-sample.txt

1) For our legal team, can you produce the signed deletion attestation template you mentioned and an abbreviated subprocessor table that lists locations only (we can keep vendor names confidential)?
2) Can we get a 30-min call tomorrow at 10am PT to walk the InfoSec team through the deletion flow and evidence? Anna will coordinate and send a calendar invite.

If you can drop the attestation and the redacted location table into the Drive link Hannah shared, that would speed review.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Sam
